title: Transatlantic Pronunciation & Stress Differences (UK vs US)

Identify stress differences in French loanwords (garage, ballet)
Apply rhoticity, bath-split, and flap differences

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Transatlantic Pronunciation & Stress Differences (UK vs US)
1. Definition: Systematic phonological, stress, and lexical differences between British (SSBE) and American (GA) English.

2. Rule: 1. Stress: French loanwords stressed on 1st syllable in UK (GArage, BALlet) vs 2nd in US (gaRAGE, balLET); advertisement /ədˈvɜːtɪsmənt/ (UK) vs /ˌædvərˈtaɪzmənt/ (US). 2. Rhoticity: GA pronounces all R sounds; SSBE drops R unless followed by vowel. 3. BATH Vowel: /ɑː/ in UK (bath, dance) vs /æ/ in US. 4. T-Flapping: US flaps intervocalic /t/ to /d/ (water).
3. Why? Divergent historical development after 17th-century settlement of North America.
4. How to recognize? Identify transatlantic variant pairs in vocabulary and accent.
5. Common examples: garage: UK /ˈɡærɑːʒ/ vs US /ɡəˈrɑːʒ/; advertisement: UK /ədˈvɜːtɪsmənt/ vs US /ˌædvərˈtaɪzmənt/; schedule: UK /ˈʃɛdjuːl/ vs US /ˈskɛdʒuːl/; bath: UK /bɑːθ/ vs US /bæθ/
6. Counter-examples: Words with identical stress and pronunciation in both dialects.
7. Exceptions: Individual speaker preference in international global English.
8. Common mistakes: Mixing British and American stress conventions inconsistently within one sentence.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: US stresses French loanwords at the END (gaRAGE); UK stresses at the START (GArage)!
10. Key vocabulary: transatlantic, SSBE, General American, rhoticity, bath-split, stress variant
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟣 C1
13. Associated Visual: 🇬🇧 British flag vs 🇺🇸 American flag over transatlantic word pairs.
14. Key Takeaway: Be consistent! Know UK vs US stress and vowel differences!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Where is stress placed in "garage" in British vs American English? (UK = 1st syllable GArage; US = 2nd syllable gaRAGE)
CCQ 2: How is "bath" pronounced in British SSBE vs American GA? (UK = /bɑːθ/ long a; US = /bæθ/ short a)
CCQ 3: What is rhoticity? (Pronouncing R in all positions, as in American GA)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Identify whether the pronunciation is UK or US variant:
🎯 Item: GArage (1st syllable stress) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: British (UK)
🎯 Item: gaRAGE (2nd syllable stress) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: American (US)
🎯 Item: schedule as /skɛdʒuːl/ ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: American (US)
